text: The richer review plan is built.
All 6 steps landed, one with a deviation,
and I made 15 calls the plan did not cover.
After each call, the video stops:
accept it, or flag it.
2 things you asked for are already here.
Each part has a numbered chip under its bar,
and N and P jump between parts.
When the video stops on a call,
A accepts it and B flags it.
Also asked for: the sound fix.
An old bug saved mute when you typed m in a comment.
The player now ignores that setting and stores mute under a new name,
instead of deleting the old one.
Step 1 landed as written.
A question can carry 2, 3 or 4 options.
3 sit in a row, 4 sit 2 by 2,
and on a phone they stack,
so the text never shrinks.
resolve plan now finds your chosen option by its letter when the label differs.
Matching the exact label only was the other way,
but real plans put the letter first,
so it never matched.
4 options sit 2 by 2 until the video is 1,200 pixels wide.
4 across on a fourteen-forty window was the other way,
but there, 4 narrow cards wrap each reason onto 4 or 5 lines.
Next, part 2: step 2, where you can tick more than one answer.
Part 2 of 5.
Up to 4 options is reported.
Now, questions where more than one answer is right.
Step 2 landed, and keeps the decision from the plan review:
one summary frame, whatever you pick.
You tick options and press Confirm.
The decision ledger stores the whole set,
and resolve plan marks every pick.
When finish project assembles the video,
a pick-all question gets no branch beats at all.
Allowing branches was the other way,
but the review chose one summary frame,
whatever is picked.
A pick-all answer is one entry in the decision ledger,
with every pick in it.
One entry per pick was the other way,
but you answered one question, and reel check compares questions.
A summary frame shows your picks in one element:
a list gets one line per pick,
anything else gets the labels with commas.
A template per item was the other way;
this rule is simpler to rely on.
On a replay, an answer with no branch of its own skips straight to
its summary.
Routing only single picks was the other way,
but then an answer in your own words replayed every branch.
Quick check.
On a pick-all question, you tick Web and Slides.
What plays next: both options' branches,
one frame listing your picks, or nothing at all?
Next, part 3: steps 3, 4 and 5.
Part 3 of 5.
Pick-all questions are reported.
Now: how many questions, words on a mark,
and diagrams.
Step 3 landed.
The budget is now one decision per part of about a minute,
not about 3 per plan.
And reel check warns, but never fails,
past 6 open questions.
Step 4 landed.
When you finish a mark, a text box opens beside it,
and the video stays paused.
Enter saves the words as the mark's comment.
After review, Escape keeps them too;
only the x in the box throws them away.
Changed after review, as you asked:
Escape now keeps what you typed,
just like clicking away, and only the x in the box throws it away.
Discarding on Escape was the old way,
but you did not want to lose your words by accident.
Step 5: the frame lint, which checks each frame as it is built,
now fails any frame with more than 6 parts.
And the style guide asks for one new thing per beat,
in plain names.
The lint counts the parts named in a frame's code,
and a whole-system beat can opt out.
Checking in a browser was the other way,
but this is cheap enough to run on every frame.
One deviation.
4 frames of the older close-the-lifecycle video now fail this rule,
with 7 and 10 parts.
I left them as they are,
instead of rebuilding them, because that video is outside this plan.
Next, part 4: step 6, what only a video can tell us.
Part 4 of 5.
Marks carry words, and diagrams stay small.
Last step: the feedback only a video can give.
Step 6 keeps the decision from the plan review:
nothing is asked of you.
The player notes each rewind of over 2 seconds,
and each slow-down.
resolve plan lists them under 'Hard to follow here',
on their step.
A rewind is a scrub or a key press that goes back more than
2 seconds.
Counting every jump back was the other way,
but clicking a step in the record is not getting lost.
Speed changes within 3 seconds merge into one,
and only slowing below normal counts.
One moment per change was the other way,
but speeding back up is no sign of trouble.
The resolved plan lists these moments by step,
with their times.
Time order was the other way,
but the revise works step by step,
and a moment is a signal,
not a comment.
Quick check.
You drag back 10 seconds to hear a step again.
Where does the agent see it:
nowhere, as a comment, or under 'Hard to follow here',
on that step?
Next, the last part: notes on your answers,
and what ran.
Part 5 of 5.
All 6 steps are reported.
Last: notes on answers, and the tests.
Also asked for in the review:
any answer can carry a note.
The box sits under the options,
and you can edit the note later,
in the record.
A note sends its step to the revise step,
which rewrites the plan, just like a comment.
Keeping notes in the record only was the other way,
but a note usually narrows the answer.
A note on its own still lets you approve at the end.
Treating it like a comment was the other way,
but a note clarifies an answer;
it does not ask for a change.
Notes are offered on plan questions only,
not on quick checks or on my calls.
A note on every stop was the other way,
but the review file defines notes on decisions only.
What ran: every test passes, including 10 new checks on the script side and
57 on the player side.
The player was also checked by screenshot at 4 widths,
in light and dark.
Not tested: no real plan video has a 4-option or pick-all question yet,
so the player was checked on a test sample.
And on a phone, a long part title can still be cut short.
That is what landed: 6 steps,
15 calls, and one deviation.
Flag any call, draw on a step to ask for a change,
or accept it.
